sections.h2: Hamilton County at a glance for sellers
sections.html:
Chattanooga, the county seat, anchors Hamilton County and the metro area of southeast Tennessee. Beyond Chattanooga, the county holds Collegedale, East Ridge, Lakesite, Red Bank, Ridgeside and Soddy-Daisy as cities, plus the towns of Lookout Mountain, Signal Mountain and Walden. Who collects your tax and at what rate depends on which of these your address falls in.

The county had 390,833 people in July 2025, 6.5 percent more than in April 2020. It has 176,983 housing units, and owners occupy 63.9 percent of them. A typical owner-occupied home is worth $312,800 and household income is $76,183. Permits for new building numbered 1,887 in 2025.

One office values, one body sets the rate, and one office collects. The assessor appraises each parcel. The commissioners choose the county rate. The Trustee mails bills and receives payments.

The Trustee sits in Room 210 of the courthouse on Georgia Avenue in Chattanooga and runs a second counter at 6125 Preservation Drive, Suite 101, in the Bonny Oaks Industrial Park. Both open from eight to four on weekdays. Call (423) 209-7270.

The Trustee also bills for Collegedale, East Ridge, Lakesite, Red Bank, Ridgeside, Soddy Daisy and Walden. Chattanooga does its own billing through the City Treasurer at City Hall, 101 E 11th Street, Room 100, at (423) 643-7262 or ptax@chattanooga.gov. A house in Chattanooga therefore gets two separate bills.

The Assessor of Property is at 6135 Heritage Park Drive, (423) 209-7300. The assessor's FAQ points out that the office only sets values. When a bill goes up and the value did not move, the cause is a higher rate.

After the four-year reappraisal, the county certified a rate of $1.51 per $100 of assessed value, replacing $2.23. The county mayor and the assessor described it as the lowest since 1941. The assessor estimated that roughly two thirds of owners would pay the same or less county tax than they did in 2024. State law forces a lower certified rate after a reappraisal so that rising values do not create a windfall, although local governments may raise it again.

Chattanooga's tax page lists a separate city rate of 1.93 per $100. Houses count at one quarter of appraised value for tax purposes, and commercial buildings at two fifths. For a Chattanooga home, the county bill and the city bill each come from assessed value over 100 times that body's rate. Phone the Trustee to learn the rate printed on this year's notice.

If your home is in Chattanooga, budget for both bills when you compare listings or estimate a buyer's monthly cost. A home in one of the other cities served by the Trustee carries the county bill plus whatever that city adds.

Bills are mailed in late September. You can pay starting October 1, and the window runs to the end of February. From March 1 the county adds 1.5 percent per month, or 18 percent a year in its own description.

The Trustee's FAQ gives practical rules:

  • You may pay in part, and the office accepts partial payments
  • For mailed checks, only a postmark by the deadline counts, and the office's own meter stamps are rejected
  • Online payments are treated as made on the day of the transaction
  • Any First Horizon Bank in the county will take a current-year payment if you bring the original bill

No state rule makes the county mail a notice, and a missing one does not erase interest. Chattanooga uses a different late schedule, charging 1 percent interest and a half percent penalty each month, and it hands unpaid earlier years to the Chancery Court in March. Taxes that stay unpaid can end up at the county's June tax sale, which carries a one year redemption period.

Talk to the appraisers first. Search your parcel with the assessor's property and sales comparison tools, or call a staff appraiser at 423-209-7990. The assessor wants informal review requests in before May 20.

Still unhappy? The assessor's office can give you the form to go before the county Board of Equalization. That board meets during June and takes filings into the first week of the month, so confirm the closing date by phone. A later stage is the State Board of Equalization, where an administrative judge hears the case. The owner has to prove the number, and matched sales of similar homes make the strongest evidence.

Hamilton County revalues on a four-year cycle. The newest values took effect in 2025. The next reappraisal is set for 2029. In the years between, an assessor can still fix mistakes in ownership, location or physical description when the owner asks before March 1.

Tennessee refunds a slice of the tax to low-income seniors, disabled homeowners and disabled military service members. The county's FAQ quotes a $37,530 income ceiling for 2025. The state's 2026 brochure raises that to $38,470 of 2025 income, with a $33,600 value cap for seniors and disabled owners and $175,000 for disabled military service members. Hamilton County says it matches what the state pays. To book a time, call the Bonny Oaks office at (423) 209-7799.

The freeze for owners 65 and older follows different lines. The county government is missing from the state's list of 28 freeze counties, yet Chattanooga adopted one in 2017 and uses a 2026 income limit of $63,470. It reduces only the city bill. For land used for farming or forestry, the assessor runs the Greenbelt program, which requires 15 acres or more.

Bills are addressed to the owner of record. Because each side's share depends on the transfer date, buyers should check the closing statement or ask the title company, and any unpaid balance stays with the parcel. As a seller, request the balance for every tax year from the Trustee's office before you list, and the city balance too if you are in Chattanooga.

Inherited the home, or behind on the bill? The title company can settle the debt from your proceeds at closing. The Register of Deeds, reachable at (423) 209-6560, records the deed and collects the state transfer tax.

faqs.q: What is the Hamilton County property tax rate?
faqs.a: The county's certified rate after the latest reappraisal was $1.51 per $100 of assessed value, replacing $2.23. Chattanooga's page shows its own city rate of 1.93 per $100. Call the Trustee at (423) 209-7270 to confirm what your bill uses.

faqs.q: When are Hamilton County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Starting October 1 and ending with February. Interest of 1.5 percent monthly begins March 1. Notices go out near the end of September, though state law does not demand them.

faqs.q: How often does Hamilton County reappraise property?
faqs.a: Every four years. The most recent was in 2025 and the next is 2029. Between reappraisals, a record error can still be corrected on request.

faqs.q: Do I pay both Chattanooga and Hamilton County property tax?
faqs.a: Yes, a Chattanooga owner gets a county bill from the Trustee and a separate city bill from the City Treasurer. The Trustee also collects for seven other cities, among them East Ridge and Soddy Daisy.

faqs.q: Is there property tax relief for seniors in Hamilton County?
faqs.a: Yes. Owners 65 or older under the income limit get a state refund, and the county matches that amount. Chattanooga adds a freeze for seniors. Call (423) 209-7799 for an appointment.
